title: Soft-card / blurry-square inventory
rule: A camera-facing soft square or disc may not stand in for a designed object. Distant background stars are the only exception, and only while they stay tiny, bright, and at sky depth. If the player can fly past it, it is not a star.

entries.playerSees: Tiny bright stars with depth in the sky
entries.technique: Point sprites with round falloff, at sky depth
entries.whyListed: This is the one place the cheap card reads as the real thing: small, bright, far away.

entries.playerSees: A few brighter star flares in the same sky
entries.technique: Distant camera-facing flare cards at sky depth
entries.whyListed: Same exception as the star field: they stay in the sky, not in the flight path.

entries.playerSees: Distant planets as round discs in the sky
entries.technique: Textured camera-facing sprites of an authored planet bake
entries.whyListed: Allowed only as a far-sky stand-in for a designed planet. Not a license to sprite a field of rocks.

entries.playerSees: A rare comet crossing the sky: flaring head, braided ion-tail filaments, dust fan
entries.technique: Far-sky camera-facing card carrying authored comet art (head + structured tail), same class as the planet impostors
entries.whyListed: Upgraded 2026-09 from a smeared gradient streak to a designed head-plus-tail painting. Still listed because it is a sky-depth impostor card, not licensed at play scale.

entries.playerSees: Shared transient impulses and compression fronts; animated smoke and combustion volumes
entries.technique: Instanced swept 3D impulse sheets and bounded ray-marched density/temperature films, with independent event progress, seed and force heading; legacy sprite API names retained
entries.whyListed: Candidate migration 2026-09-07 removes the camera-facing silhouette carrier. The scan still finds the compatibility API. Isolated WebGL frames and 140 focused tests are not normal-game or integrated-GPU acceptance; see VFX_UPGRADE_2026-09-07.md. Do not mark accepted from the method name or geometry alone.

entries.technique: Shared radial-gradient texture used by stars and by every halo sprite
entries.whyListed: The factory that makes the blurry square. Stars may keep using it. World objects may not.

entries.playerSees: Nothing; a clipped 1x1 loading/Continue pass only uploads live drawable buffers
entries.technique: Type-matched Three.js proxy, including Points, rendered with color writes disabled
entries.whyListed: The completeness scan finds Points and gl_PointSize, but this is an offscreen GPU-admission mechanism rather than a world object or player-facing effect.

entries.playerSees: Nothing on the live route (spaceBackground replaced this)
entries.technique: Point sprites with a round texture
entries.whyListed: Dead path. Do not revive it as a world-object renderer.

entries.technique: Sprite plumes and halos used as teaching examples
entries.whyListed: The lab still teaches the banned cheat as if it were the production method.

entries.playerSees: Small tier icons floating on scanned rocks in the mining UI
entries.technique: Camera-facing sprites with an authored badge texture
entries.whyListed: UI chrome, not the rock. Keep off the world-object list.
